title.narrative: Strengthened capacity of member States to ratify and apply international labour standards and to fulfil their reporting obligations

description.narrative:
Iraq has been a member of the ILO since 1932 and has ratified several ILO Conventions, including nine out of ten fundamental Conventions (C029, C087, C098, C100, C105, C111, C138, C182, C187) and three out of four Governance Conventions: (C081, C122, C144) in addition to 60 out of 176 Technical Conventions. Most recently, in 2023 the ILO played a pivotal role in guiding the ratification process of the ILO Social Security (Minimum Standards) Convention, 1952 (No. 102), and the Maritime Labour Convention, 2006 (MLC, 2006). These conventions, officially ratified by the Government of Iraq in March 2023, are set to come into force in March 2024. The ILO remains committed to providing ongoing technical support to the Iraqi government and social partners in fulfilling reporting commitments for the application of these conventions.

The Government of Iraq on a recent decision to ratify Convention 190 on Violence and Harassment in the world of work will bring Iraq to be the first country in the region to join the convention. The ILO is committed to support the Government and its social partners to fulfil the ratification process of this Convention.
